what: BBB Foods runs Tiendas 3B, a chain of small hard-discount grocery shops in Mexico selling a limited range of mostly own-brand products at very low prices.
customers: Lower and middle income Mexican households shopping for groceries close to home.
money: food and household goods, mostly own-brand
moat: A hard-discount model with few product lines per category, which gives enormous buying power per item and lets it undercut traditional Mexican grocers and convenience chains.
risks: A $104M net loss while hundreds of new shops are opened
The analyst average target is right where the shares trade
Rapid store opening is expensive and each shop takes time to mature
opportunities: Revenue grew from $1.1B to $4.3B in four years and is $5.3B over the last twelve months
$247M of free cash flow despite the expansion
Hard discount has only a small share of Mexican grocery, far below its share in Europe
watch: New store openings and same-store sales growth.
